_comment: Phase 5 (issue #24, EPIC D #4) baseline tool config. VERIFIED shape: fabric_iq_preview is the Foundry server-side tool (docs/verified-capabilities.md §2a; Learn foundry/agents/how-to/tools/fabric-iq, updated 2026-07-03). project_connection_id (REQUIRED) is the id of the Fabric IQ (OneLake Catalog) project connection created in the Foundry portal; server_url is the Ontology MCP endpoint for the live iqnpl_ontology. BOTH come from config/env (.env) — never committed (Art. VI: infra GUIDs are OK, but the connection id is resolved at runtime from FABRIC_IQ_PROJECT_CONNECTION_ID). Tool-optimization target (§3b): the optimizer may refine the DESCRIPTION only, never type/required/defaults. Per Art. IV the description names business concepts, not tables/columns/SQL.

tools.description: Answer questions about the water-quality / algal-bloom domain by querying the Fabric IQ ontology (preview). Ask in business terms about monitored water sites and their attributes (location, region, water-body type, whether active); water-quality measurements taken at those sites (readings such as pH, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, chlorophyll-a, nutrients, and algal cell counts); the algae species observed (scientific and common name, taxonomic group, toxicity level, bloom triggers); and the remediation treatments applied at sites (method, outcome, follow-up). You can also ask how these relate: which measurements and treatments belong to a site, and which algae species is dominant in a measurement. Fabric IQ resolves the question via NL2Ontology over the bound OneLake data and returns a grounded answer in the signed-in user's context. Use it for every data-backed claim; do not invent table or column names.
